subject: Microburst profiling for deploy-mode decision — post-call next steps
snippet: Recap of call: microburst spikes to 1.2k qps for 3-5s, need profiling + pilot to decide Hosted vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rj.patel@fastcheckout.com>, FastCheckout Infrastructure <infra@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Microburst profiling for deploy-mode decision — post-call next steps

Hi Rajesh / FastCheckout infra team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to see the traffic shape. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can converge on Hosted vs Dedicated for your checkout path: 

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Baseline steady-state ~200 qps for normal checkout flows.
- Short, recurring microbursts up to ~1.2k qps lasting roughly 3–5s that coincide with promotions and certain cart flows.
- Strong sensitivity at p95/p99 for customer-facing latency (you mentioned >2s at p99 during bursts).

Why this matters for deploy-mode:
- Hosted API can be tuned (pre-warming, prefix/KV caching, autoscale) but sustained multi-second microbursts to 1.2k qps may trigger throttling or cold-path overhead unless we reserve capacity.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) gives predictable headroom to keep tail latency low during bursts, but comes with a committed cost profile.
- Private VPC usually only needed for compliance / data residency — not required based on what you shared.

Proposed immediate plan (pilot-focused, low-friction):
1) You send 24–72 hours of anonymized request traces / aggregated QPS by second + a short list of representative prompt lengths (we attached microburst_profile.csv as an example format).
2) Redwood runs a microburst replay to characterize p50/p95/p99 tail impact on Hosted autoscale vs a Dedicated 8-GPU pool. We will include KV/prefix caching in the Hosted run.
3) Based on replay results we provide: recommended deployment mode, expected tail latencies, and a cost delta estimate for the pilot window.
4) Pilot options: a 2-week Dedicated pilot (mirror traffic) or a Hosted pilot with pre-warm and short reserved burst capacity. We can include a promotional credit for the Dedicated pilot to reduce your upfront cost.

Attachments: microburst_profile.csv (format), pilot_scope.docx (draft scope).

Can you confirm: (a) you can share the request traces (or a sanitized sample) by end of day tomorrow, and (b) whether you lean toward trying a Dedicated pilot (we’ll scope 8 GPUs) vs starting on Hosted with burst reservations?

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Priyom to prepare cost and runbook once we have the traces.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
(Attachment: microburst_profile.csv)
(Attachment: pilot_scope.docx)
From: Rajesh Patel <rj.patel@fastcheckout.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microburst profiling for deploy-mode decision — post-call next steps

Thanks Mina — that matches what we see. A couple clarifications: 
- Baseline is ~200 qps, microbursts spike to ~1.2k qps for ~3–5s, and these occur roughly every 12–18 minutes during promo windows.
- p99 currently climbs above 2s during those spikes.

We will extract and sanitize 48 hours of per-second QPS and example payload sizes and share by EOD tomorrow.

Quick ask: ballpark for Dedicated 8-GPU monthly number you’d use for an initial pilot (so I can flag procurement)? Not expecting exact yet — just a range.

Onward — Rajesh

Subject: Re: Microburst profiling for deploy-mode decision — cost/ops notes

Adding quick internal notes for the pilot and procurement ask.

Cost framing: for a Dedicated pilot we typically size on the peak sustained seconds during microbursts. For the pattern Rajesh described (1.2k qps for 3–5s), an 8-GPU pool (A100x or equivalent) is a reasonable starting point for throughput headroom and to keep p99 sub-500ms depending on prompt lengths and KV cache hit rates.

Proposed commercial offer for FC-3129 pilot:
- 2-week Dedicated pilot: 50% pilot discount on committed hours (we can convert to credits in the first invoice).
- If they choose Hosted pilot first, offer 2 weeks of increased burst reservation plus evaluation SLA for tail latency.

Action items (internal):
- Priyom: prepare a quick replay harness and baseline script to run against the sanitized traces once Mina drops them.
- Mina: draft the customer-facing pilot scope and include the promotional credit; I can prep a short cost worksheet for procurement.

Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rj.patel@fastcheckout.com>, FastCheckout Infrastructure <infra@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Microburst profiling for deploy-mode decision — confirmed next steps and timeline

Rajesh — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline below so we all have the same expectations: 

1) You share sanitized per-second QPS traces + two representative prompt payloads (any S3/Drive link is fine) — target: EOD 2027-09-30.
2) Priyom will run the replay and return a short results sheet (p50/p95/p99 for Hosted vs Dedicated with caching toggles) within 48 hours of receiving traces.
3) Ben will produce a pilot cost worksheet and proposal for the two pilot flavors (2-week Dedicated pilot w/ credit or Hosted pilot w/ burst reservation) within 24 hours of results.
4) We aim to have an internal decision and pilot start date by Oct 4, 2027.

Links: HubSpot deal record — https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FC-3129
Drive folder for uploads — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

If that timeline looks good, please confirm and upload the traces. Once we have them we’ll run the replay and follow with measured latency & cost tradeoffs so you can pick the right deploy mode.

Thanks — Mina
